data.name: Mahendri
data.gender_notes: Mahendri is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit words 'maha' meaning great and 'indra' referring to the king of gods. The name Mahendri carries the meaning “Great Indra” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Mahendri usually hope their child will grow to embody great indra and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of divine power and leadership.
data.etymology: Mahendri belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Great Indra.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mahendri total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Mahendri" is rooted in ancient Indian tradition and holds a deep cultural significance as it is derived from the auspicious names of two revered deities - Lord Mahadev (Shiva) and Lord Indra. The name invokes the power, strength, and royalty associated with these gods, making it an evocative and prestigious name for an individual in Hindu culture.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, Lord Mahadev (Shiva) is considered the supreme god and the destroyer of all negative energies and imperfections. In essence, he represents transformation and pure growth. Lord Indra, the king of gods, is the god of rain and thunder, symbolizing the power and strength of nature. Thus, the name "Mahendri" carries the divine blessings of these deities in the spiritual realm, bringing a sense of strength, achievement, and transformation to the individual bearer.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Mahendri: Mountain of Self-realization. This name evokes the inner journey towards self-discovery and enlightenment, symbolized by the towering peak of a mountain.

vedic_reference.note: Not found in Vedas or Upanishads, but derived from Sanskrit

historical_references.reference: Mahendra I (r. 613-632 CE) was a Chalukya king who ruled the 'Deccan Plateau' in southern India. His reign marked the golden age of Chalukya power, and he expanded the empire's territories through military campaigns.

Mahendravarman I (r. 571-630 CE) was a Pallava king of the 'Early Chola' period in Tamilakam, South India. He is considered a great patron of arts and architecture, and his monuments include the famous 'Mamallapuram Shore Temple'.
